html:
The Batepá massacre began on 3 February 1953 on São Tomé, when Portuguese colonial forces and armed settlers killed hundreds of local Creoles, known as forros.

The governor, Carlos Gorgulho, wanted the forros to work on the cocoa estates as contract labourers, work they saw as slavery. Rumours of a revolt led to days of arrests, torture and killing, with victims beaten, burned or drowned.

The killings turned many islanders against Portugal, and the movement that later won independence grew from them. 3 February is Martyrs Day, a national holiday. It showed how the cocoa estates were still run, half a century after the labour scandal.
sum: The Batepá massacre began on 3 February 1953 on São Tomé, when Portuguese colonial forces and armed settlers killed hundreds of local Creoles, known as forros.
